review_findings: Read the full native source, wrapper, contract, build file and CPU schedule checks. The 512-row wave assigns all per-core up pairs before any down waits. Each down M tile waits for its actual I producer set; there is no wait for a padded or empty producer.

AIV0 processes all actual rows in eight-row batches; AIV1 is idle. FIX_S precedes GU publication, MTE3_S precedes activation publication and S_MTE2 follows ready consumption. These explicit fences require hardware validation; source review does not establish GM visibility or physical progress.

Canonical BF16 GU, activation and unweighted Z are retained with independent buffers. W1[4,2I,H] and W2[4,H,I] are viewed as column-major operands without a weight conversion. No gating, division by gate, SHMEM, gradient or optimizer operation has been added.

Flags have two channels and a 128-byte stride per pair, are zero-initialized privately per invocation and are never recycled within the invocation. CPU coverage and dependency-graph checks cover tails, empty experts, skew and the target, but do not execute native code.

The wrapper bounds allocations, checks canonical layouts, dtype, device and aliasing, and records all seven tensors on the actual launch stream. The component live-byte cap is not a whole-device memory bound.

BlockMmad reuse across K=H and K=I, hard-event token interactions, mixed-kernel core mapping and early AIV1 return remain runtime questions. A successful compile will not resolve them. P0/P1/P2/P3 remain frozen.
